source.title: The Rules-and-Facts Model for Simultaneous Generalization and Memorization in Neural Networks
source.authors: Gabriele Farn'e; Fabrizio Boncoraglio; Lenka Zdeborová

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether models can memorize random factual labels while generalizing on clean rule labels, and refines the claim by showing trade-offs that depend on model capacity, kernel geometry, regularization, and learned representations. Its synthetic task uses partially random labels rather than fully random labels on the whole training set.
record.gate_note: The paper tests a rules-and-facts task: a fraction ε of training labels are random, and it measures error on those examples and generalization error on clean teacher labels. It does not test fully random labeling of the entire training set or test error at chance under that condition. Cited results about fitting random labels are not rows. Figure-only curves are recorded without estimating values from plots.
record.test_reason: The end-to-end CNN experiments test memorization of a random-label subset alongside clean-label generalization in a new mixed-data setting. They bear narrowly on V4 at approximately 20% random labels. The main kernel and frozen-representation trade-offs do not establish the claimed corruption-dependent behavior of standard deep networks.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. More precisely, the authors identify kernel geometries allowing optimal generalization and perfect factual recall together, and report that learned deeper representations mitigate the trade-off on CIFAR10-RAF. They do not establish that depth alone causes this behavior or explain how training constructs the favorable representations.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a mixed structured-rule/random-fact task, high-dimensional theory for linear, random-feature and kernel estimators, and CIFAR10-RAF experiments with learned CNN representations. It does not reproduce the original fully randomized-label experiments or their training recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome depends on regularization λ, kernel geometry (µ1/µ⋆), random-feature width κ, and whether the CIFAR10-RAF representation is random or learned; the four-layer learned representation retains perfect factual recall at its best test point, while the two-layer learned representation retains a residual trade-off.

fits_no_version.finding: Nonlinear kernels interpolate random facts in the ridgeless limit; capacity, kernel geometry, bandwidth, and ridge regularization govern factual-recall versus generalization trade-offs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fixed-feature and kernel estimators can simultaneously memorize random training labels and generalize, with the achievable trade-off depending on capacity and geometry.

fits_no_version.finding: Learned four-layer features retain perfect factual accessibility at the best-test ridge readout, whereas two-layer features retain a residual trade-off.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature learning can produce representations in which random factual associations remain linearly accessible while clean generalization improves.

record.problems: The theoretical analysis is a simplified Gaussian teacher-rule/random-fact setting. CIFAR10-RAF results are qualitative, figures carry several values without textual numbers, and some end-to-end positive-regularization runs reached the epoch cap before the stated plateau criterion. The learned-representation experiment does not establish that depth alone caused the progression.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-bearing results omitted. Figure-only values were retained only where the study reports distinct conditions; no numerical estimates were read from plots. The many theoretical parameter sweeps in Figures 1, 3–5, 8–9 and 12–16 are not separately enumerated because the text provides qualitative conclusions or aggregate claims rather than separately stated condition-level outcomes, and the relevant general results are represented in R1–R2.

untested.parts: Standard deep networks trained on entirely random labels with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, including chance test performance. The theoretical model includes ε=1, contrary to the record's blanket statement that fully random labeling is never considered.
Relative training time for true and random labels, and convergence slowdown as corruption increases.
The same standard networks fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs. Gaussian inputs in the kernel theory do not establish this claim.

A standard deep-network sweep from no corruption to completely random labels, perfect fitting of the entire training set throughout, and steadily increasing test error toward chance. The empirical CNN experiments fix the random-label fraction near 0.2 and evaluate factual error separately.
The stated fully random-label regularization comparison, dropout and data augmentation interventions, and generalization on true labels after removing explicit regularization.
Training trajectories showing shared real-label patterns learned before random labels.

record.verdict_notes: The record overstates what the trade-off results imply for V4: that version does not promise perfect recall at the generalization-optimal regularization. Forgetting after readout regularization therefore does not itself justify limits_scope. Epoch-capped optimization is an evidential limitation, not a demonstrated boundary of the phenomenon. The quoted AI conversation is not study evidence.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not train on a completely random labeling of the entire training set or measure test error at chance in that setting.
Training time and convergence rate as label corruption increases are not measured.
Shuffled pixels, permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs are not tested.

The study varies the fraction of random labels and measures clean-rule generalization and error on random-label examples, but it does not report total training-set error across the full none-to-all corruption sweep or establish a steadily rising test-error curve for standard deep networks.

The paper varies ridge/readout regularization and includes a qualitative end-to-end weight-decay control, but does not test dropout or data augmentation as interventions on fitting fully random labels, nor whether removing those methods alone harms true-label generalization.
The paper does not track training dynamics to determine whether rule patterns are learned before random labels.

rows.subject: kernel regression
rows.operation_detail: ERM on RAF labels with a fraction ε of randomly labeled examples; square loss; λ→0+
rows.locator: Appendix C.3.1, Eq. (183) and preceding text
rows.note: Asymptotic theoretical result; this is error on the random-label subset, not total training error.
rows.check: Zero factual error is correctly reported, but this is an asymptotic kernel interpolation result, not the stated deep-network corruption experiment. It cannot establish V4.

rows.subject: kernel regression
rows.operation_detail: ERM on RAF labels; square loss; optimized positive regularization
rows.measure: Memorization error on random-label examples at the generalization-optimal regularization
rows.baseline: zero memorization at λ→0+ for nonlinear kernels
rows.value: zero for t≤tmemopt(ε); strictly positive for t>tmemopt(ε), where t=µ1/µ⋆
rows.note: The result qualifies simultaneous fitting by kernel geometry; it does not report total training error.
rows.check: The result concerns kernel geometry and generalization-optimal ridge regularization. V4 does not assert that selecting optimal test performance preserves interpolation.

rows.subject: random features regression
rows.size_stated: finite width κ=p/d; tested κ values 0.5, 1, 2, 10, 50, 100 and κ→∞
rows.operation_detail: Square-loss regression with erf activation; regularization swept
rows.note: The authors state perfect memorization is possible only for κ large enough; precise curve values are not stated.
rows.check: This aggregates width and regularization trade-offs for fixed random features at one corruption fraction. The text establishes a capacity threshold qualitatively, but not a listed version.

rows.subject: random features regression
rows.size_stated: finite width κ=p/d; tested κ values 0.5, 1, 2, 10, 50, 100 and κ→∞
rows.operation_detail: Hinge-loss regression/classification with ReLU activation; regularization swept
rows.note: The authors state perfect memorization is possible only for κ large enough; precise curve values are not stated.
rows.check: This aggregates fixed-feature capacity and regularization trade-offs at one corruption fraction, rather than measuring the claimed deep-network behavior as corruption increases.

rows.subject: RBF kernel ridge regression
rows.operation_detail: Square-loss KRR with regularization swept on CIFAR10-RAF
rows.uncertainty: averages over 20 repeated random draws; no error bars stated
rows.note: The text reports a qualitative comparison and says bandwidth choices shift the errors; exact curve values are only in the figure.
rows.check: RBF kernel regularization and bandwidth trade-offs at fixed corruption do not establish V4. The numerical curves are unavailable in the supplied text representation.

rows.subject: wide two-layer CNN, learned representation
rows.stage_stated: representation learned for 800 epochs, then frozen readout
rows.operation_detail: Network trained on CIFAR10-RAF at zero explicit regularization with square loss; affine readout then ridge-fit
rows.measure: Random-label factual error at the test-optimal readout
rows.baseline: randomly initialized representation has a substantial fraction of random labels forgotten at its best test point
rows.value: improves both test performance and factual recall; trade-off does not disappear completely
rows.uncertainty: five-seed means shown; no numeric value stated in text
rows.note: Textual result; readout is an exact convex optimum after the representation is frozen.
rows.check: The outcome measures factual accessibility after freezing learned features and refitting a ridge readout. Residual forgetting at the test-optimal readout does not demonstrate failure of the original network to fit noisy training labels.

rows.subject: parameter-matched four-layer CNN, learned representation
rows.stage_stated: representation learned for 800 epochs, then frozen readout
rows.operation_detail: Network trained on CIFAR10-RAF at zero explicit regularization with square loss; affine readout then ridge-fit
rows.measure: Random-label factual error at the test-optimal readout
rows.uncertainty: five-seed mean solutions; no numeric uncertainty stated in text
rows.note: Authors also report that the unregularized readout combines substantially better test performance with perfect factual recall.
rows.check: Perfect factual classification is correctly reported for the refitted readout, but this row measures accessibility in frozen learned features. It does not report total training error or corruption-dependent degradation.

rows.subject: wide two-layer CNN, random representation (frozen RF-CNN)
rows.size_stated: feature dimension p=14204; network has approximately 2.74×10^6 trainable parameters
rows.operation_detail: Affine ridge readout trained on fixed random representation; regularization swept
rows.measure: Random-label factual error at the test-optimal readout
rows.value: forgets a substantial fraction of them at best test performance
rows.uncertainty: five-seed mean solutions; no numeric uncertainty stated in text
rows.check: This is a fixed random-feature readout control. Forgetting at the best-test ridge penalty is not evidence against the listed fitting claims.

rows.subject: pre-activation WRN-16-4, learned representation
rows.stage_stated: representation learned for 400 epochs, then frozen readout
rows.operation_detail: Network trained on CIFAR10-RAF at zero explicit regularization with square loss; affine readout then ridge-fit
rows.measure: Random-label factual error along learned-representation readout path
rows.baseline: random representation does not interpolate randomized labels at λ=0
rows.uncertainty: figure reports five-seed mean and 95% CI
rows.note: The text describes additional controls but does not state the learned WRN factual-error values.
rows.check: The row concerns a frozen-representation ridge path; learned WRN factual-error values cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text.

rows.subject: two-layer CNN, end-to-end weight-decay sweep
rows.operation_detail: Joint training with square loss and quadratic penalty on all trainable variables
rows.value: figure only; some positive-λ points near apparent test minima reached the epoch cap
rows.uncertainty: five-seed mean and 95% CI in figure
rows.note: Appendix describes the tendency qualitatively and flags incomplete optimization at some points.
rows.check: End-to-end noisy-label training bears on V4's fitting component at one corruption level, but the supplied text gives no architecture-specific factual-error outcome for this two-layer sweep. Epoch-capped runs further limit interpretation.

rows.subject: four-layer CNN, end-to-end weight-decay sweep
rows.operation_detail: Joint training with square loss and quadratic penalty on all trainable variables
rows.value: learned deeper models can retain zero factual error through the range in which test error improves
rows.uncertainty: five-seed mean and 95% CI in figure; several positive-λ points near test minima reached epoch cap
rows.locator: Appendix E.6, Figure 18 and accompanying text
rows.note: Authors characterize this as a qualitative control; some runs did not meet the objective plateau criterion.
rows.check: The text explicitly reports zero factual error for learned deeper models while test error improves. This supports the fitting component at fixed corruption; it does not establish total training interpolation or the full corruption sweep. Some positive-penalty runs were epoch-capped.

relationships.condition: End-to-end learned deeper CNNs on CIFAR10-RAF with approximately 20% random-label automobiles, over the reported penalty range retaining zero factual error
relationships.reason: R11 reports zero random-subset classification error while clean test error improves; this supports simultaneous signal learning and noise memorization at this corruption level, subject to the stated optimization caveat.
relationships.display_finding: Random-subset classification error remained zero while clean test error improved across the reported penalty range, subject to the stated optimization caveat.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: four-layer learned CIFAR10-RAF representation at the minimum-test-error readout
reader_labels.reason: The readout still classifies every randomized example correctly (R7).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: kernel methods and shallower or fixed representations
reader_labels.reason: Fact recall trades off against clean-rule generalization depending on regularization, kernel geometry, width, and representation; perfect recall is not retained in all settings (R2-R6, R8).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The qualitative result favors learned deeper models, but several points near apparent test minima reached the epoch cap, limiting interpretation (R10-R11).
